Hear’s a breakdown of the image data provided,describing what the code represents:
Overall:
This code snippet shows HTML figure elements,each containing an img tag. These are used to display images on a webpage. The images are from an article on nshoremag.com about the Red Jacket beach Resort. The code is structured to provide responsive images , meaning the browser will choose the most appropriate image size based on the user’s screen size and resolution. Detailed Clarification:
: This is the container for the image.
class="wp-block-image size-large" : Indicates this is an image block (likely from WordPress) and is designated as a “large” size.
: This is the actual image tag.
decoding="async" : Tells the browser to decode the image asynchronously,which can improve page load performance.
width="..." and height="..." : Specifies the dimensions of the image in pixels.
data-id="..." : A unique identifier for the image, likely used by the content management system (WordPress in this case).
alt="" : The alternative text for the image. This is important for accessibility (screen readers) and SEO. Currently,all alt attributes are empty,which is not ideal. They should describe the image content.
class="wp-image-... lazyload" : WordPress image class and a class for lazy loading (images are loaded only when they are visible in the viewport).
src="... “: The URL of the main image file.
srcset="... “: This is the key to responsive images. It provides a list of image URLs with different widths. The browser will choose the most appropriate one based on the device’s screen size and pixel density.for example: https://www.nshoremag.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Red-Jacket-Beach-Resort-exterior-Heidi-Kirn-Photography-_0532-1024x768.jpg 1024w means the image at that URL is 1024 pixels wide.
data-sizes="auto" : Specifies how the image should be sized relative to the viewport. auto means the browser will determine the appropriate size.
data-eio-rwidth="..." and data-eio-rheight="..." : Data related to an image optimization plugin (likely “ShortPixel”).
data-eio="l" : Another attribute related to the image optimization plugin. sizes="(max-width: 1024px) 100vw, 1024px" : This attribute, used with srcset , tells the browser how the image will be displayed at different screen sizes. (max-width: 1024px) 100vw : If the screen width is 1024 pixels or less, the image should take up 100% of the viewport width ( 100vw ).
1024px : Otherwise (screen width is greater then 1024px), the image should be displayed at a width of 1024 pixels. Images Shown:
